mechanism_note: Its own 5' leader uORFs make ATF4 translation a textbook eIF2-alpha-phosphorylation-driven translational-efficiency switch (more of the existing mRNA pool translated under stress), not primarily a transcriptional induction event.

Direct ATF4 transcriptional target; correlates more with proliferation/biosynthesis genes than with the terminal-UPR gene block at the whole-panel correlation level, plausibly because its induction is more transcription-driven than ATF4's own switch.
Same pattern as ATF3 -- direct ATF4 target, correlates with the growth/biosynthesis gene block rather than the terminal-UPR block.

CHOP; single leader uORF but works via an elongation-stall/ribosome-bypass mechanism rather than the standard short-uORF-reinitiation model most count-based uORF models assume -- flagged as a 'hidden uORF candidate' (residual -82.6pts vs. count-model expectation) likely because the count model does not capture this atypical mechanism.

Classic HIF1A/hypoxia transcriptional target; this atlas's #1 consensus-ranked gene shows clean-CDS usage DECREASING under ISR/ER-stress conditions despite well-established transcriptional induction under hypoxia -- working hypothesis is a translational throttle layered on top of real transcriptional induction, not a contradiction of the transcript-level literature.

Same pattern as LDHA -- correctly signed as a Hypoxia up-gene but shows positive (not negative) correlation with OXPHOS at the translation level, the opposite of the expected transcript-level Warburg-effect direction.

Has a real, literature-documented uORF inside an IRES element (AUG 852, 186nt upstream of main ORF) that is known to be translationally induced under global cap-dependent-translation shutoff (documented for hypoxia/ischemia). This atlas's pooled data shows MORE leader-uORF engagement and flat/slightly-less clean-CDS usage specifically under viral infection -- a translational throttle on top of VEGFA's well-known transcriptional induction during infection/inflammation, not derepression as first (incorrectly) concluded.

m6A writer; this atlas's ribosome-profiling-derived values show its knockdown elevates a full interferon-stimulated-gene translation signature (not just transcription) in 2 of 3 independent studies -- consistent with literature on m6A loss causing 'viral mimicry' via MDA5-sensed endogenous dsRNA, now shown to hold at the translation level specifically.

ac4C writer; knockdown/knockout elevates the Senescence/SASP translation score consistently, matching literature on NAT10 protecting HeLa cells from senescence-inducing stress. Evidence currently limited to one lab/cell line.

Was used as a Baseline/housekeeping reference gene but shown to have negative correlation with the rest of the housekeeping panel; it is a well-documented interferon-stimulated gene at the transcript level, so its instability here is expected, not a translation-specific finding -- removed from the Baseline module.
Same as B2M -- ubiquitin C is itself stress-inducible, so its removal from the Baseline housekeeping module reflects a known transcript-level property, not a new translation-specific observation.
